body.translated_text: <s>Kedārabhaṭṭa</s>: <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s>, with <s>Sulhaṇa</s>'s <s>Sukavihṛdayānandinī</s>
First Chapter

children.text: saśrīkaṃ prabhayā yutaṃ rucirayā prodbhāsitaṃ gaṅgayā
children.translated_text: Endowed with <s>Śrī</s> (splendor), possessed of beautiful radiance, illuminated by <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
resplendent with many faces, adorned with the crest of the crescent moon,
accompanied by noble ones, always worshipped with garlands by all <s>gaṇas</s> (attendants) who have assembled —
victorious is the body of <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord Śiva), venerated by the three worlds, like the science of prosody (<s>chandaḥśāstra</s>)!
In the lineage (<s>gotra</s>) of <s>Kṛṣṇātreya</s>, there was born long ago a foremost among southerners,
named <s>Velāditya</s>; his brilliant son was a fine poet,
whose son, named <s>Sulhaṇa</s>, composed upon the <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s>,
a commentary on meters with elegant verses, named <s>Sukavihṛdayānandinī</s> (Delighter of Good Poets' Hearts).

body.translated_text: Salutations to <s>Sarasvatī</s>.

children.translated_text: For the attainment of happiness and progeny, having bowed to <s>Śaṃkara</s> (Śiva) who is worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Acyuta</s> (Viṣṇu),
who is accompanied by <s>Gaurī</s> and <s>Vināyaka</s> (Gaṇeśa), who bestows auspiciousness upon the world —
There was a foremost among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> named <s>Pavyeka</s>, learned in the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> and the <s>Śaiva śāstras</s>;

children.text: tasya putro 'sti kedāraḥ śivapādārcane rataḥ // KVrk_1.2 //
children.translated_text: his son is <s>Kedāra</s>, devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>'s feet.
By him is composed this work on prosody (<s>chandas</s>), equipped with examples and definitions,
named <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> (Ocean of Gems of Meters), for the easy understanding of beginners.

body.translated_text: At the commencement of the treatise, the author states, preceded by salutation to the chosen tutelary deity, the subject-matter and purpose of the treatise, in three verses:

body.text: vedānāmarthā vedārthāḥ / śivo devatā yeṣāṃ tāni śaivāni śāstrāṇi / vedārthāśca śaivaśāstrāṇi ca tāni jānātīti sa tathoktaḥ ya

children.translated_text: by name, devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>'s feet, is his son.
by <s>Kedāra</s>, this work with the definitions to be stated —
is the arrangement of fixed syllables, <s>mātrās</s> (morae), and <s>gaṇas</s> (metrical feet); equipped with both of these —

children.text: / vṛttāni śrīprabhṛtīni tānyeva ratnāni teṣāmākara utpattisthānam / kimarthaṃ /
children.translated_text: The <s>vṛttas</s> (meters) such as <s>Śrī</s> and others — these themselves are the gems; their <s>ākara</s> (mine) is the place of origin. For what purpose?
Attainment with ease is <s>sukhasiddhi</s>; for that <s>sukhasiddhi</s>. Of whom?
of those of limited understanding. Having done what?
to <s>Mahādeva</s> (the great god). Of what description?

children.text: lokānāṃ śaṃ sukhaṃ karotīti lokaśaṃkarastam / punaḥ kathaṃbhūtam /
children.translated_text: He who makes <s>śam</s> (happiness) for the worlds, that is <s>Lokaśaṃkara</s>. Again, of what description?
worshipped by <s>Viraṃci</s> (Brahmā) and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> (Viṣṇu). Again, of what description?

children.text: gaurī ca vināyakaśca gaurīvināyakau tābhyāṃ upetaṃ saṃyutam / kimartham /
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurī</s> and <s>Vināyaka</s> together are <s>Gaurīvināyaka</s>; accompanied by them, that is, joined with them. For what purpose?
For the attainment of happiness and progeny (<s>sukhasaṃtānasiddhyartham</s>) —

children.text: / sukhaṃ paraṃ brahmānandātmakaṃ saṃtānaḥ putrapautrādi tayoḥ siddhiḥ prāptistadarthaṃ sukhasaṃtānasiddhyartham /
children.translated_text: Happiness is supreme bliss, of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>; <s>saṃtāna</s> is sons, grandsons, etc.; the attainment of both of these — for that purpose, <s>sukhasaṃtānasiddhyartham</s>.
having prostrated — this is the syntactic connection. The qualifier extends over three verses. || 1-3 ||

body.translated_text: The meanings of the <s>Vedas</s> are <s>vedārthas</s>; the <s>śāstras</s> whose deity is <s>Śiva</s> are <s>Śaiva śāstras</s>; he who knows both the meanings of the <s>Vedas</s> and the <s>Śaiva śāstras</s> is thus described. He who is

children.translated_text: That which was stated by teachers such as <s>Piṅgala</s> and others, which is secular (<s>laukika</s>), of two kinds,
distinguished by <s>mātrā</s> (mora) and <s>varṇa</s> (syllable) — that prosody is described here.

body.translated_text: He now states what is meant by the word <s>chandas</s> (prosody):

children.translated_text: That which by <s>Piṅgala</s> and other teachers,
the proponents of the science of prosody,

children.text: loke bhavaṃ na vaidikaṃ / kāvyādiṣu tasyānupayogāt /
children.translated_text: occurring in worldly usage, not Vedic; because it has no application in <s>kāvya</s> (poetry) and such works.
of two varieties. When asked 'how?', it is answered:

children.text: tyāha / mātrābhedena āryādi varṇabhedena śrīprabhṛti vṛttabhedeneti || 4 ||
children.translated_text: by the distinction of <s>mātrā</s>: <s>Āryā</s> and others; by the distinction of <s>varṇa</s>: <s>Śrī</s> and others; by the distinction of <s>vṛtta</s> (meters). || 4 ||
Of this prosody bound in six chapters, the extent is clearly to be known

body.translated_text: Now he states the number of verses in the work:

children.translated_text: and they have the definitions to be stated: designations, <s>mātrā</s> meters, <s>samavṛtta</s> (even meters), <s>ardhasamavṛtta</s> (half-even meters), <s>viṣamavṛtta</s> (uneven meters), and the six <s>pratyayas</s> (operations) —
is to be known as one hundred and thirty-six.

body.translated_text: That which is studied — these are

children.text: samastaṃ vāṅmayaṃ vyāptaṃ trailokyamiva viṣṇunā // KVrk_1.6 //
children.translated_text: all that is verbal is pervaded, just as the three worlds are pervaded by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.translated_text: Now he states the <s>gaṇas</s> (metrical feet):

children.translated_text: '<s>ga</s>-<s>la</s>' — by merely taking the first syllable, the terms <s>guru</s> (heavy) and <s>laghu</s> (light) are grasped;
even the totality of verbal expression (<s>śabdabrahma</s>) —
All heavy is <s>ma</s>; initial and medial light are <s>ya</s> and <s>ra</s>; final light are <s>sa</s> and <s>ta</s>;

children.text: gmadhyādyau jbhau trilo no 'ṣṭau bhavantyatra gaṇāstrikāḥ // KVrk_1.7 //
children.translated_text: medial and initial heavy are <s>ja</s> and <s>bha</s>; three light is <s>na</s>; these eight <s>gaṇas</s> (metrical feet) are groups of three.

body.translated_text: He states the definition of each of these individually:

children.translated_text: Initial and medial light are <s>ya</s> and <s>ra</s> —

children.text: mukhamādi aṃtarmadhyaṃ ādau madhye laghū yayostau mukhāntarlau yagaṇaragaṇau ( ^ _ _, _ ^ _) /
children.translated_text: The initial is the beginning, the medial is the middle; those in which the light syllables are at the beginning and middle respectively are the <s>ya-gaṇa</s> and <s>ra-gaṇa</s>: ( ˘ _ _, _ ˘ _ ).

children.text: / aṃte avasāne gurulaghū yayostau sagaṇatagaṇau yathā ( ^ ^ _, _ _ ^) /
children.translated_text: Those in which the heavy and light are at the end — these are the <s>sa-gaṇa</s> and <s>ta-gaṇa</s>, thus: ( ˘ ˘ _, _ _ ˘ ).
Medial and initial heavy are <s>ja</s> and <s>bha</s> —

children.text: / guru madhye ādau yayostau jagaṇabhagaṇau yathā ( ^ _ ^, _ ^ ^) /
children.translated_text: Those in which the heavy is in the middle and at the beginning — these are the <s>ja-gaṇa</s> and <s>bha-gaṇa</s>, thus: ( ˘ _ ˘, _ ˘ ˘ ).
The <s>na-gaṇa</s> has three light syllables, thus: ( ˘ ˘ ˘ ). These <s>ma</s>, <s>ya</s>, <s>ra</s>, <s>sa</s>, <s>ta</s>, <s>ja</s>, <s>bha</s>, <s>na</s> —

children.text: varṇavṛttagaṇā bhavantītyarthaḥ / mātrāgaṇānāṃ vakṣyamāṇasūtre vidhānāt / caturgurvādīnāmapi gaṇādisaṃjñā mā bhūdityāśaṃkya niyamannāha /
children.translated_text: they are the <s>gaṇas</s> of syllabic meters (<s>varṇavṛtta</s>) — this is the meaning. Since <s>mātrā-gaṇas</s> (mora-based feet) will be prescribed in the sūtra to follow. Lest it be suspected that the designation <s>gaṇa</s> etc. applies also to groups of four heavy syllables and such, he specifies the delimitation:

children.text: iti trayaḥ parimāṇaṃ yeṣāṃ te trikā iti || 7 ||
children.translated_text: those whose measure is three, they are <s>trikāḥ</s>. || 7 ||

body.translated_text: In this science of prosody, the one in which all syllables are heavy (<s>guru</s>) —

children.translated_text: The <s>gaṇas</s> in this system are to be known as having four <s>kalās</s> (time-units), with heavy syllables at the end, middle, beginning, and all positions,
along with four light syllables — five such <s>gaṇas</s> are established in <s>Āryā</s> and other meters.

body.translated_text: Now he states the <s>mātrā-gaṇas</s> (mora-based metrical feet):

children.translated_text: With heavy syllables at all positions, beginning, middle, and end —

children.text: sarve ca te ādiśca madhyaṃ ca antaśca sarvādimadhyāṃtāsteṣu guravo yeṣāṃ te sarvādimadhyāntaguravaḥ /
children.translated_text: All, and the beginning, and the middle, and the end — these are <s>sarvādimadhyānta</s>; those in which the heavy syllables are at these positions are <s>sarvādimadhyāntaguravaḥ</s>.
One with <s>anusvāra</s> (nasal), one ending in <s>visarga</s>, a long vowel, and one followed by a conjunct consonant —

children.text: vā pādāntastvasau gvakro jñeyo 'nyo mātṛko lṛjuḥ // KVrk_1.9 // iti /
children.translated_text: and optionally one at the end of a <s>pāda</s> (verse-quarter) — that is a <s>guru</s> (heavy), marked as curved; any other <s>mātrā</s>-bearing syllable is a <s>laghu</s> (light), marked as straight.
That which occurs with an <s>anusvāra</s> is
By the word '<s>ca</s>' (and), one ending in a consonant is also included.
A quarter (<s>pāda</s>) of a verse, composed of a measured number of syllables and <s>mātrās</s>, arranged in <s>gaṇas</s>, having the definition to be stated —

children.text: vartamāno laghurapi vibhāṣayā guruḥ syāt / sa ca kavisamayavyavahārāt dvitīyacaturthayoreva pādayorante veditavyaḥ / yathā /
children.translated_text: a light syllable occurring there may optionally be heavy. And this, by the convention of poets, is to be understood only at the end of the second and fourth <s>pādas</s>. For example:

body.translated_text: For the purpose of recognizing heavy and light syllables, he says:

body.text:
prāyaḥ samāsannaparābhavānāṃ dhiyo viparyastatamā bhavanti /
asaṃbhave hemamayasya jantostathā 'pi rāmo lulubhe mṛgāya // iti /
body.translated_text: Generally, the minds of those nearing destruction become inverted in their darkness; even so, <s>Rāma</s> was lured by the deer, though the existence of a golden creature was impossible.

body.text:
tathā ca /
‘śriyaḥ patiḥ śrīmati śāsituṃ jagajjagannivāso vasudevasadmani'; ityādi dṛṣṭavyam /
sa ca prastāre

children.translated_text: Having established this, he states the definition of light:
'Any other <s>mātrā</s>-bearing syllable is light, marked as straight' —

children.text: / anusvarādirahito anyo mātṛko ekamātro varṇo laghurbhavati / sa ca prastāre ṛjuḥ saralaḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: A syllable devoid of <s>anusvāra</s> and the rest, another <s>mātrā</s>-bearing syllable — a single-<s>mātrā</s> vowel — is light. And in the <s>prastāra</s> it is <s>ṛju</s> (straight). || 9 ||

body.translated_text:
And likewise: '<s>Śriyaḥ patiḥ</s> (the lord of <s>Śrī</s>), in the auspicious abode of <s>Vasudeva</s>, to rule the world, the world-dwelling one' — and so on, should be examined.
And in the <s>prastāra</s> (metrical expansion), that is marked as

body.text: yuktaparāśca ya ityanena prāpte gurutve apavādamāha /

children.translated_text: A consonant cluster at the beginning of a word (<s>pada</s>) is called <s>krama</s> (sequence);
by such a preceding cluster, even a heavy syllable may sometimes become light.

body.translated_text: Since heaviness is obtained by 'followed by a conjunct consonant,' he states the exception:

children.translated_text: occurring at the beginning of that word, whichever
by the <s>krama</s> occurring before, the syllable occurring at the end of the preceding word, though having obtained
according to the requirements of the meter. Now, what is this

children.text: ucyate / pūrvācāryāṇāṃ piṃgalanāgaprabhṛtīnāṃ kālidāsādīnāṃ ca kavīnāṃ samayaḥ parigṛhītaḥ / saṃyogaḥ kramasaṃyogaḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: The convention of earlier teachers — <s>Piṅgala</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, and others — and of poets such as <s>Kālidāsa</s> has been adopted. A consonant cluster is a <s>krama-saṃyoga</s> (sequential cluster). || 10 ||

body.translated_text: A word (<s>pada</s>) ending in an inflectional suffix —

children.text: taruṇaṃ sarṣapaśākaṃ navaudanaṃ picchalāni ca dadhīni /
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, a young man of the village enjoys a delicious meal of fresh mustard greens, new-cooked rice, and slimy curds,

body.translated_text: In that case,

children.text: tava hriyāpahriyā mama hrīrabhūt śaśigṛhe 'pi hṛtaṃ na dhṛtā tataḥ /
children.translated_text: By your modesty my modesty was stolen; even in the house of the moon it was taken, not held; therefore —

children.text: vahalabhrāmarameṣakatāmasam mama priye kva sa yeṣyati tatpunaḥ //
children.translated_text: With the great buzzing of bees, dark — where will he go, my beloved? And again —

body.translated_text: Thus:

children.translated_text: The drowsy one falls from modesty; fallen from modesty, he loses his energy;
without energy, he is humiliated; from humiliation, he comes to despondency;
despondent, he grieves; overcome by grief, he falls from his wits;
bereft of wits, he perishes — alas, death is the abode of all calamities!

body.text:
mamaiva te hṛte / yathā /
snehādgehādbhujagatanayālokakautūhalena sthūlottuṃgastanabharalasanmadhyabhaṃgānapekṣāḥ /
paurā nāryastaralanayanānandamutpādayantyo dhāvanti sma drutamapahriyaḥ sraṃsamānottarīyāḥ // iti /
bodhapradīpe 'pi yathā /

children.translated_text: Those by whose sacrifices this earth, the sustainer of beings, was adorned at every step,
by whom, having conquered this circle of the world, it was given to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> —
even they, in this ocean of heavy existence, having assumed the sport of bubbles,

children.text: dhṛtvā dhṛtvā sapadi vilayaṃ bhūbhujaḥ saṃprayātāḥ //
children.translated_text: those kings have suddenly gone to dissolution.

body.translated_text:
'Of me indeed was it taken.' For example:
Out of affection, from the house, eager to see the snake-girls (the <s>Nāga</s> maidens), regardless of the bending of their waists heavy with great towering breasts, the city women, producing delight in restless eyes, ran swiftly, their upper garments slipping off.
Also in the <s>Bodhapradīpa</s>, for example:

body.text:
śiśupālavadhe yathā /
prāptanābhihṛdamajjanamāśu prasthitaṃ nivasanagrahaṇāya / iti /
body.translated_text:
In the <s>Śiśupālavadha</s>, for example:
'Having quickly reached the navel, sinking to the chest, setting forth to seize the garment' — thus.
With a <s>bhra</s>-cluster, for example:

children.translated_text: 'O moon-faced one! This bee, thinking it a lotus' — surely, to you —
having abandoned the vine's blossoms, desires to drink.

body.text:
tathā ca /
bhramati bhramaramārīkānane vipramukte / ityādi /

children.translated_text: Among the flowers of the wish-fulfilling tree, among the lotuses of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s>, upon the temples of the elephants of the gods, in the tresses of the heavenly maidens —

children.text: sthitaśayitavibuddhaprītikaste bhramo 'yaṃ bhramasi bhramara yena tvaṃ mudhā ketakeṣu //
children.translated_text: in standing, lying, and waking, your delight is this delusion: you wander, O bee, vainly among the <s>ketaka</s> flowers!

body.translated_text:
And likewise:
'The swarm of bees wanders in the garden, having been released' — and so on.

children.translated_text: 'At the beginning of a word' — why this specification? So that it does not apply elsewhere.

children.text:
asamagravilokanena kiṃ te dayitaṃ paśya varoru nirviśaṃkā /
na hi jātu kuśāgrapītamambhaḥ sucireṇāpi karotyapetatṛṣṇam // iti
children.translated_text: What use is an incomplete gaze? O beautiful-thighed one, look at your beloved without hesitation! For indeed, water sipped from a blade of <s>kuśa</s> grass never quenches thirst even after a long time.

body.translated_text: With an <s>hra</s>-cluster, for example:

body.text:
‘ājahratustaccaraṇau pṛthivyāmi'ti /
tathā ca /
pradyotasya priyaduhitaraṃ vatsarājo 'tra jahre /
body.translated_text:
'They seized those two feet from the earth' — thus.
And likewise:
<s>Pradyota</s>'s beloved daughter was seized here by the king of <s>Vatsa</s>.
With a <s>bhra</s>-cluster, for example:

body.text:
kundāvadātairbhavato yaśobhiḥ śubhrīkṛtaṃ kiṃ paramāravīra /
adyāpi yadbibhrati kālimānamarātinārīvadanotpalāni // ityādi /
body.translated_text: By your fame, white as <s>kunda</s> flowers, the world has been purified, O great hero! Why then do the lotus-eyes of enemy women still bear their darkness even today? — and so on.

children.translated_text: 'Sometimes' — why this word? So that it does not apply everywhere.

body.translated_text: With a <s>gra</s>-cluster, for example:

children.translated_text: 'The earth, from the stamping of feet, suddenly goes to a state of doubt;
the position of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — broken by the iron-bar-like arms that wander' — thus.

body.translated_text: With a <s>bhra</s>-cluster, for example:
'There the six-legged one (bee) wanders vainly indeed' — thus.

children.translated_text: Some interpret '<s>padādāu</s>' (at the beginning of a word) differently. That is incorrect,
because the sūtra and the example cannot be reconciled.

children.text:
/
tathāpi /
taruṇaṃ sarṣapaśākaṃ navodanaṃ picchalāni dadhīni /
alpavyayena suṃdari grāmyajano miṣṭamaśnāti / ityudāharaṇamāryayā pradarśitam / āryāyāṃ pādavyavasthā nāsti / pūrvārdhottarārdhagrahaṇāt pūrvārdhottarārdhamityāryālakṣaṇaṃ kurvāṇo granthakāra evaṃ jñāpayati / tāvadāryāyāṃ pādavyavasthā nāsti paiṃgalīyasūtrapāṭhācca / svarā 'rdhañcāryārdhamiti /
children.translated_text:
Nevertheless—
'Young mustard greens, freshly cooked rice, and slimy curds—
with little expense, O beautiful one, the village folk eat delicious food.'
This example has been shown using an <s>Āryā</s> (meter). In the <s>Āryā</s>, there is no fixed arrangement of <s>pāda</s>-s (metrical feet). By using the terms 'prior half' and 'latter half,' the author, formulating the definition of the <s>Āryā</s> as 'prior half and latter half,' indicates this: there is indeed no fixed <s>pāda</s> arrangement in the <s>Āryā</s>. This is also confirmed from the <s>Paiṅgalīya Sūtra</s> reading: 'A <s>svara</s> (vowel) and a half constitute an <s>Āryā</s> half.'
Therefore the reading is '<s>padādau</s>' (at the beginning of a foot).
The better reading is simply thus—enough said on this topic. || 11 ||
The technical names for 'ocean,' 'element,' '<s>rasa</s>,' etc. should be known from common usage.
A <s>pāda</s> is known as one-fourth; <s>yati</s> is the term for a caesura. // <s>KVrk</s> 1.12 //

body.translated_text: Now he states the technical terms (<s>saṃjñā</s>):

body.text: tadyathā / catvāro 'bdhivedāḥ / pañca śarendriyāṇi / ṣaṭcartavaḥ / sapta svararṣayaḥ / aṣṭau vasavaḥ / nava naṃdarandhrāṇi / daśa diśāḥ / ekādaśa rudrāḥ / dvādaśādityāḥ / trayodaśa viśvedevāḥ / caturdaśa bhuvanāni / pañcadaśa tithaya ityādi /
body.translated_text: Namely: four = oceans/Vedas; five = arrows/senses; six = seasons; seven = notes (<s>svara</s>)/sages (<s>ṛṣi</s>); eight = <s>Vasu</s>-s; nine = <s>Nanda</s>-s/apertures; ten = directions; eleven = <s>Rudra</s>-s; twelve = <s>Āditya</s>-s; thirteen = <s>Viśvedeva</s>-s; fourteen = worlds (<s>bhuvana</s>); fifteen = <s>tithi</s>-s (lunar days), and so forth.

children.text: / vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇasya vṛttasya caturthāṃśo bhāgaḥ pādasaṃjño bhavet /
children.translated_text: one-fourth portion of a <s>vṛtta</s> (verse) whose definition will be stated hereafter is designated by the term <s>pāda</s>.

body.translated_text: He states the definition of a <s>pāda</s> (metrical quarter):

children.translated_text: <s>Yati</s> is the term for a break (<s>viccheda</s>)—

"<s>Yati</s> occurs everywhere at the end of a <s>pāda</s>, and especially at the half-verse;
and at the end of a word following an 'ocean-number' etc., whether the case-ending is manifest or unmanifest;

// End of the <s>Upasthitapracupita</s> Section //
That prosody which has quarter-verses of unequal syllables, or quarters that are unequal, like the <s>Daśadharma</s>,

body.text: yacchaṃdo noktamatra gātheti tatsūribhiḥ proktam // KVrk_5.12 //
body.translated_text: and which is not stated here — that is called <s>Gāthā</s> (song) by the learned.

children.text: yadevameva aṣṭau daśasaptanavākṣaraṃ vā sarvapādairasamaṃ tripādaṃ ṣaṭpādaṃ vā
children.translated_text: that which is thus: having eight, ten, seven, nine syllables, or unequal in all quarters, three-quartered, six-quartered, or the like —

children.text:
/ yathā /
daśa dharmaṃ na jānanti dhṛtirāṣṭra nibodha tān /
mattaḥ pramatta unmattaśśrāṃtaḥ kruddho bubhukṣitaḥ /
tvaramāṇaśa bhīruśca lubdhaḥ kāmī ca te daśaḥ // iti ṣaṭpadī gāthā /
ityevamādi asmin cchaṃdasyarthe noktaṃ prayogeṣu dṛśyate tadgātheti vidvadbhiruktam /
children.translated_text:
For example:
'Ten do not know <s>dharma</s> — know them, O <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>: the intoxicated, the heedless, the insane, the exhausted, the enraged, the hungry, the hasty, the cowardly, the greedy, and the lustful — these ten.' This is a six-versed <s>gāthā</s>.
Thus and so on — what is not stated in this treatise on prosody but is seen in actual usage, that is called <s>gāthā</s> by the learned.

children.text: prabhṛti tatsarvaṃ gāthāsaṃjñamavagantavyam / chaṃdasāmānaṃtyātpratipadamabhidhātumaśakyaṃ tatsarvasaṃgrahaṇīyaṃ ekā saṃjñā kṛteti || 12 ||
children.translated_text: and so on — all of these are to be understood as bearing the designation <s>gāthā</s>. Since meters are infinite, it is impossible to name each one individually; therefore, this one designation was created to encompass them all. || 12 ||

body.translated_text: Those whose syllables are unequal — such quarter-verses; that in which they occur —

body.text: iti sulhaṇaviracitāyāṃ sukavihṛdayānandinyabhidhānāyāṃ vṛttaratnākaracchaṃdovṛttau viṣamavṛttādhyāyaḥ paṃcamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, on uneven meters (<s>viṣamavṛtta</s>), in the <s>Vṛttaratnākara Chandovṛtti</s>, the commentary entitled <s>Sukavihṛdayānandinī</s> composed by <s>Sulhaṇa</s>.

Sixth Chapter
The Chapter on the Six Operations (<s>Ṣaṭpratyaya</s>)
<s>Prastāra</s> (Metrical Expansion)
<s>Prastāra</s> (expansion), <s>Naṣṭa</s> (recovery of a lost meter), <s>Uddiṣṭa</s> (identification), <s>Ekadvyādilaghukriyā</s> (the procedure of one light, two light, etc.),

body.text: saṃkhyā caivādhvayogaśca ṣaḍete pratyayāḥ smṛtāḥ // KVrk_6.1 //
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃkhyā</s> (counting), and <s>Adhvayoga</s> (path-combination) — these six are the recognized operations (<s>pratyayas</s>).

children.translated_text: In a <s>pāda</s> that is all heavy, below the first <s>guru</s>, place a <s>laghu</s>;

children.text: yathopari tathā śeṣaṃ bhūyaḥ kuryādamuṃ vidhim // KVrk_6.2 //
children.translated_text: whatever is above, do the same for the rest — repeat this procedure.
In positions that are deficient, place <s>gurus</s> — continue until the entire line is all light.
This is called the <s>prastāra</s> (metrical expansion), by those who know the investigation of meters.

body.translated_text: Now he states the six operations for the meters that have been described:

children.text: yāvatāṃ varṇānāṃ vṛttasya pādastāvaṃta eva guravo vilikhyante / yathā / caturakṣaracchaṃdasi ādyā
children.translated_text: As many syllables as a meter's <s>pāda</s> has, that many heavy syllables are written. For example, in a four-syllable meter, from the first —

children.text: adhovibhāge laghuṃ varṇaṃ nyasya sthāpayitvā tadanaṃtaraṃ nyastalaghoḥ sakāśāt śeṣebhyo varṇebhyo adhaḥ kiṃ sthāpyata ityāha /
children.translated_text: in the lower portion, having placed a light syllable, then from the position of that placed <s>laghu</s>, what is placed below the remaining syllables? He says:
'Whatever is above, do the same for the rest' —

children.text: / yadyupari gurustadā adhastādapi gururyadyupari laghustadā adhastādapi laghuḥ śeṣam / upari tulyo dīyate ityarthaḥ / tena laghoranaṃtaraṃ trīṇi gurūṇī sthāpyante /
children.translated_text: If above there is a <s>guru</s>, then below also a <s>guru</s>; if above there is a <s>laghu</s>, then below also a <s>laghu</s> — for the rest. What is above is given as equal — this is the meaning. Therefore, after the <s>laghu</s>, three <s>gurus</s> are placed.

children.text: / laghuṃ nyasya guroradhaḥ yathopari tathā śeṣamiti punarapyamuṃ vidhiṃ kuryāt / yadā upari gururbhavati laghuṃ nyasya guroradha iti vidherabhāvādyaḥ pūrvadeśā
children.translated_text: place a <s>laghu</s> below a <s>guru</s>, and do the same for the rest as above — repeat this procedure. When there is a <s>guru</s> above, since the rule 'place a <s>laghu</s> below a <s>guru</s>' does not apply, whatever position from the previous
the deficient position is filled with <s>gurus</s> — this is the meaning.
by this method, the placement should be continued
until the entire line is all light.
The <s>pāda</s> becomes all <s>laghu</s>. That which is expanded is

children.text: varṇānāṃ vinyāsaviśeṣaḥ / evaṃ caturakṣarapāde ṣoḍaśavṛttāni bhavanti / chaṃdāṃsi vilīyante asyāmiti
children.translated_text: a particular arrangement of syllables. Thus in a four-syllable <s>pāda</s>, there are sixteen meters. That in which meters are investigated (<s>vilīyante</s>) is

body.translated_text: <s>Naṣṭa</s> (Recovery of a Lost Meter)

children.text: naṣṭasya yo bhavedaṃkaḥ tasyārdhe 'rdhe same ca laḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever the number of the lost meter may be — when halved and halved, if it is even, a <s>laghu</s>;
if odd, adding one, then halving and halving — a <s>guru</s> results.

body.translated_text: Now, to explain the <s>naṣṭa</s> (recovery), he says:

body.text: prastāradarśitānāṃ vṛttānāṃ madhye yadvṛttaṃ naṣṭaṃ luptaṃ bhavati tasya

children.translated_text: 'Whatever the number of the lost meter' —
the sequential number starting from one —

children.text: / yathaitasmiṃścaturakṣare chaṃdasi paṃcamaṃ vṛtaṃ naṣṭam / tasya aṃkaḥ paṃca sa ca ardhaṃ na prayacchati / saikaḥ kriyate tadā ṣaḍbhavanti / te ardhaṃ kriyante / ardhitāstrayo bhavanti / tadardhe guruḥ prāpyate punastrayo 'rdhaṃ na prayacchanti / saikāścatvāraḥ / te 'pi ardhastadardhe punarlabdho gurudvayoḥ samatvāt / tadardhe laghuḥ prāpyate punareko 'rdhaṃ na prayacchati / saikordvyaḥ tadardhe punarapi gurureva labhyate / itthaṃ naṣṭasyodāharaṇam / tathā ca / ādyau dvau gurū tābhyāṃ parako laghustato gururiti / '; '; / '; etaccaturakṣare chaṃdasi paṃcamaṃ vṛttaṃ bhavati || 4 ||
children.translated_text: For example: in this four-syllable meter, the fifth meter is lost. Its number is five, and it does not yield a half. So one is added, making six. That is halved; halved, it becomes three. At that half, a <s>guru</s> is obtained. Again, three does not yield a half. Adding one makes four. Halved again, the result is two — a <s>guru</s>, since both are even. At that half, a <s>laghu</s> is obtained. Again, one does not yield a half. Adding one makes two. Halving that, once again only a <s>guru</s> is obtained. Thus is the example for the lost meter. And so: the first two are <s>gurus</s>; after them, the third is a <s>laghu</s>; then a <s>guru</s>. This is the fifth meter in the four-syllable prosody. || 4 ||

body.translated_text: Among the meters shown in the <s>prastāra</s>, whichever meter is lost (<s>naṣṭa</s>), that is, obliterated —
<s>Uddiṣṭa</s> (Identification)

children.translated_text: For the identified meter, starting from the first, write doubled numbers above;

children.text: laghusthā ye tu tatrāṃkāstaiḥ saikairmiśritairbhavet // KVrk_6.5 //
children.translated_text: those numbers that stand at <s>laghu</s> positions — with one added to each, combined, give the result.

body.translated_text: To explain the <s>uddiṣṭa</s> (identification), he says:

body.text: kenacittadvṛttaṃ prastāryakatamat iti saṃkhyāparijñānā uktaṃ taduddiṣṭamucyate / pūrvatra vṛttaṃ na jñāyate / ataḥ saṃkhyayā naṣṭamuddhriyate / atra punarvṛttaṃ jñāyate saṃkhyā na jñāyate ataḥ saṃkhyāparijñānārthaṃ uddiṣṭamidamucyate / tasya uddiṣṭavṛttasya prathamādakṣarādārabhya upari

children.text: naṃkān samālikhet / yathā / asminneva caturākṣare chaṃdasi ekaṃ vṛttaṃ uddiṣṭaṃ tasya dvau varṇau gurū tato laghustato 'pi guruḥ / tatra uddiṣṭe vṛtte laghuni tiṣṭhantīti laghusthā ye punaraṃkāścatvāraḥ taiścaturbhiḥ saikaiḥ ekena sahitaiḥ paṃcabhiruddiṣṭaṃ bhavet / uddiṣṭasaṃkhyā bhavet / caturakṣarāyāṃ jātau tatpaṃcamaṃ vṛttaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: numbers are to be written. For example: in this same four-syllable meter, one meter is identified — its two syllables are <s>guru</s>, then <s>laghu</s>, then <s>guru</s>. In that identified meter, those numbers that stand at a <s>laghu</s> position — four such — these four, with one added to each, making five — the identification yields five. The identification number would be five. In the four-syllable class, it would be the fifth meter — this is the meaning. || 5 ||

body.translated_text: When someone asks 'what is this meter's number in the expansion?' — to know that number, this <s>uddiṣṭa</s> is taught. In the former case, the meter is not known; hence the <s>naṣṭa</s> recovers it from the number. Here, however, the meter is known but the number is not; hence this <s>uddiṣṭa</s> is taught for determining the number. Of that identified meter, starting from the first syllable, above —
<s>Ekadvyādilaghukriyā</s> (Procedure of One Light, Two Light, etc.)

children.translated_text: The syllables born of the meter, with one added, placed in top-to-bottom order,
are to be cast, one by one in sequence from one upward, one above another.
One should return from the penultimate, discarding one by one from above;
above the first <s>guru</s> — thus is the procedure of one light, two light, etc.

body.translated_text: To explain the <s>ekadvyādilaghukriyā</s> (procedure of one light syllable, two light syllables, etc.), he says:

children.translated_text: the syllables born of the meter —

children.text: ekasahitānyathā / caturakṣarajātau catvāro ye varṇāstān saikān paṃca / auttarādharyataḥsthitān uparyuparibhāvena sthitān
children.translated_text: that is, one more; in the four-syllable class, the four syllables plus one make five. Placed in top-to-bottom order, that is, arranged from top to bottom,
these are cast above, one above another —

children.text: nena prakāreṇa kasmādiyaṃ ekadvyādilagukriyāṃ pravartata ityāha /
children.translated_text: by this method — why does this procedure of one light, two light, etc. proceed? He says:

children.text: riti uparisthitān ādyādguroḥ / ko 'rthaḥ / sarvaguruvarṇavṛttasakāśāt ityarthaḥ / ādyaṃ kila sarvagurvakṣaramekaṃ vṛttaṃ parikalpate / etacca prastāre darśitaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: above the first <s>guru</s> that is situated above. What is the meaning? From the meter consisting of all heavy syllables — this is the meaning. For indeed, the first is reckoned as the one meter of all heavy syllables. And this is shown in the <s>prastāra</s>, as:

body.translated_text: As many as

children.translated_text: 'In a <s>pāda</s> that is all heavy, below the first, place a <s>laghu</s>' —
<s>ekadvyādilaghukriyā</s> (procedure of one light, two light, etc.)

children.text: pravartate / tatra paṃcasu varṇeṣu uttarādharabhāvena sthāpiteṣu adhaḥsthita ekastaduparisthe nikṣipyate / sa ca tathaiva tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: proceeds. There, among the five syllables placed in top-to-bottom order, the one at the bottom is cast upon the one above it. And it stays there just so,

children.text: iti vīpsavaśādekadaiva sthitimaṃtareṇa nikṣiptatvāt punarnikṣepabhāvādekaikatyāgaśca na saṃbhavati tasmātsvarūpeṇa sthita eva upari kṣipyate / tato dvitīye sthāne dvau varṇau bhavataḥ tau tṛtīyena kṣipyeta tatra trayo bhavanti / tacca caturthe nikṣipyante te catvāro bhavanti / ‘
children.translated_text: by force of the distributive usage, since it is cast at the first position itself without intermediate placement, and since there is no re-casting, the discarding of one by one does not apply; therefore, it stays in its own form and is cast above. Then in the second position there are two syllables; those are cast upon the third — there become three. And those are cast upon the fourth — they become four.
'One should return from the penultimate, discarding one by one from above' —

children.text: uparitanamekaṃ tyajyate tatra na kṣipyate ityarthaḥ / vīpsā ta eva adhobhāgāt punarnikṣepe kriyā pravartate tena adhaḥsthita eva eko dvitīye sthāne nikṣipyate tatra ca trayo bhavanti / tacca tṛtīye nikṣipyante tatra ṣaṭbhavanti upari ekaṃ tyajannivarteta / ādyaṃ ekaṃ vṛttaṃ sarvaguruḥ tasmāddekadvyādilagukriyā pravartete / tata ekaḥ sarvaguruḥ catvāri dvilaghūni ṣaṭtrilaghūni catvāri caturlaghūni ekaṃ sarvalaghuḥ eṣā lagukriyā sarvalaghuprastāreṇa pratīyate asyāstu eṣa eva kramaḥ paṃcākṣarādivṛtteṣvapi || 6-7 ||
children.translated_text: One above is discarded—meaning it is not placed there. By repetition, the operation proceeds again with placement from below: thus one already placed below is placed in the second position, and there become three. And those are placed in the third position, and there become six, discarding one above each time. The first single verse is all-heavy (<s>sarvaguru</s>). From that, the operation of making one, two, etc. syllables light proceeds. Thus: one all-heavy, four with two light syllables, six with three light syllables, four with four light syllables, and one all-light. This <s>laghukriyā</s> (light-syllable operation) is understood through the all-light expansion (<s>prastāra</s>). And the same procedure applies for five-syllable verses and beyond. || 6-7 ||

body.translated_text: Enumeration (<s>saṅkhyāna</s>)
He states the method for enumeration (<s>saṃkhyā</s>):
[The collection of numbers from the <s>laghukriyā</s> (light-syllable operation) becomes the enumeration when combined;

children.translated_text: or the sum of the numbers of the designated verse, plus one, generates this. // <s>KVrk</s> 6.8 //]

children.text: bhavet / iyaṃ tāvaddhāraṇaṃ syāt / tathā ekaścatvāraḥ ṣaṭcatvāraḥ ekameṣāmekīkṛtā vai ṣoḍaśa bhavanti caturakṣarajātau prastāryamāṇāyāṃ ṣoḍaśa vṛttāni bhavantītyarthaḥ / sa ca prastāraḥ pūrvameva vyākhyātaḥ /
children.translated_text: This much should be retained. Namely: one, four, six, four, one—when these are unified, they become sixteen. This means that when the four-syllable class is expanded, there are sixteen possible verses. And that expansion has already been explained above.

children.text: saṃkhyām / yathā / caturakṣarajātau dviguṇā ye aṃkā uparyāropitāsteṣāṃ samāhāraḥ paṃcadaśa saikaḥ ṣoḍaśeti || 8 ||
children.translated_text: enumeration. For example: in the four-syllable class, the numbers that are placed above, doubled, their aggregate is fifteen, plus one makes sixteen. || 8 ||

body.translated_text:
He states an alternative method:
The numbers above the designated verse, doubled—their
The <s>adhvan</s> (path/extent) operation

children.translated_text: The enumeration itself, doubled and minus one, is declared by the learned as the extent (<s>adhvan</s>);
one should make the finger-measure extent of a verse, and likewise a finger's breadth below. // <s>KVrk</s> 6.9 //

body.translated_text: He states the method for the extent (<s>adhvan</s>):
In the four-syllable class, the sixteen—

body.text: adhunā punarapi kaviranvayapūrvakaṃ pitrā saha sātmānaṃ nirddiśati /

children.translated_text: In the lineage of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, there was born one of manifest assemblage of virtues, a knower of the <s>Śaiva Siddhānta</s>,
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Pavya</s> alone, of exceedingly pure intellect in the understanding of <s>Śaiva</s> doctrine. // <s>KVrk</s> 6.10 //
<s>Kedāra</s>, his son, with mind single-pointedly devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>'s pair of feet,
composed this delightful work on metrics called <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s>. // <s>KVrk</s> 6.11 //

body.translated_text: Now the poet once again introduces himself along with his lineage and his father:

children.text: kaśyaṃ somaṃ pibatīti kaśyapaḥ kaśyapaśabdena yadyapi surā evābhidhīyate kathyate / tathāpyatra somamucyate surāpānasya brāhmaṇe dije niṣiddhatvāt anvayārthena vaṃśārthena kranuyāyitvamuktaṃ syāt (?) / śivasya ete
children.translated_text: '<s>Kaśyapa</s>' means 'one who drinks <s>kaśya</s> (soma)'; although by the word <s>kaśyapa</s>, <s>surā</s> (liquor) is indeed what is denoted, nevertheless here <s>soma</s> is meant, since liquor-drinking is prohibited for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. By the sense of lineage, descent in the family line is indicated (?). Of <s>Śiva</s>, those who belong to <s>Śiva</s> are

children.text: / ‘vida-vicāraṇe'; ityetasya rūpaṃ na punaḥ ‘vida-jñāne'; / tasyāśakyatvāt / yo hi vicārayati cintayati so avaśyaṃ vetti nahyaviditaṃ vicārayituṃ śaknoti viśeṣeṇa pratipūrayati svargāpavargādikāni sa
children.translated_text: This is the form from the root '<s>vid</s>' meaning 'to deliberate,' not from '<s>vid</s>' meaning 'to know'—because the latter would be impossible. For he who deliberates and contemplates necessarily knows; one cannot deliberate upon what is unknown. He who especially fulfills the goals of heaven, liberation, and so on is
a <s>vipra</s> (learned brāhmaṇa) of exceedingly pure intellect—

children.text: vimalā vistīrṇā taralā manoharā matiryasya atiśayena vimalamatiḥ / kva /
children.translated_text: <s>Vimalā</s> means pure, extensive, brilliant, captivating—he whose intellect is such to an extraordinary degree. Where?
In the understanding of the <s>Śaiva</s> scriptures.

children.text: nāmā tasya putraḥ śivaḥ śānto devatāviśeṣaḥ tasyārādhanaṃ tatra ekāgraṃ tanniṣṭhaṃ cittaṃ yasya saḥ / tathā
children.translated_text: named thus, his son. <s>Śiva</s> is the tranquil one, a particular deity; worship (<s>ārādhana</s>) of Him—in that, single-pointed, devoted—he whose mind is such. And so,

body.text: iti paṃḍitaśrīsulhaṇaviracitāyāṃ sukavihṛdayānandinyabhidhānāyāṃ chaṃdovṛttau ṣaṭpratyayādhyāyaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, the chapter on the six <s>pratyaya</s>-s (combinatorial operations), in the commentary on metrics called <s>Sukavihṛdayānandini</s> composed by the learned <s>Śrī Sulhaṇa</s>.

children.translated_text: May there be good fortune for the scribe!

children.text: vasuyugme ....... śuklaśca paṃcamyāṃ haṃsarājena muninā 'likhaṭṭīkā manoramā //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vasuyugma</s> (eighth pair) ....... on the fifth of the bright fortnight, by the sage <s>Haṃsarāja</s>, this delightful commentary was written.
